zh: 一个 IP 的出现次数只增不减：第一次 ADD 后它是唯一的，第二次 ADD 后就永远不再唯一。所以把唯一 IP 按首次出现顺序排好后，失去唯一性的 IP 只会被永久剔除，不会重新加入。
给每个不同 IP 按首次出现的顺序编号并记录出现次数，再维护一个只向前移动的指针 p，表示“可能是答案的最早编号”。编号小于 p 的 IP 都已出现至少两次，永远不会再成为答案。
ADD 时用哈希表查编号，新 IP 追加到顺序数组末尾，次数加一。FIRST_UNIQUE 时，只要编号 p 的次数 ≥ 2 就让 p 后移；停下后若 p 没越界就输出该 IP，否则输出空行（空答案也要占一行）。指针总共最多移动“不同 IP 数”次；大小写不同的 IP 是不同的键，输出要逐字节一致。
en: An IP's visit count only ever grows: after its first ADD it is unique, and after its second ADD it is never unique again. So if you list the unique IPs in order of first appearance, an IP that loses uniqueness is removed for good and never comes back.

Number each distinct IP in order of first appearance and keep its visit count, plus a pointer p that only moves forward, marking the earliest number that could still be the answer. Every IP numbered below p has appeared at least twice and can never be the answer again.

On ADD, look the IP up in a hash map; a new IP is appended to the order array, and its count goes up by one. On FIRST_UNIQUE, move p forward while the IP numbered p has count ≥ 2; when it stops, print that IP if p is in range, otherwise print an empty line (an empty answer still takes a line). The pointer moves at most as many times as there are distinct IPs in total; IPs that differ in case are different keys, and the output must match byte for byte.

explanationEn:
## Problem

The server receives commands in order. ADD ip records one visit from ip; FIRST_UNIQUE asks: among all visits so far, which of the IPs that appeared exactly once appeared earliest; if there is none, the answer is the empty string. Output the answer to each FIRST_UNIQUE in order, one answer per line, with the empty string printed as an empty line.

## Key observation

An IP's visit count only increases. When it is ADDed for the first time its count is 1 and it becomes "unique"; after its second ADD the count becomes 2, and from then on it is never unique again. So if the "unique IPs" are listed in order of first appearance, an IP that loses uniqueness is only ever removed permanently and never added back.

## Algorithm

Number each distinct IP in order of first appearance, record its visit count, and maintain a pointer p to "the earliest number that may be the answer". On a query, keep moving p forward while the IP numbered p has count ≥2; when it stops, if p is not out of range, the answer is that IP, otherwise the empty string.

## Correctness

Invariant: every IP numbered below p has count ≥2, so it is never a unique IP. The IPs the pointer skips during a query have count ≥2 and likewise can never become the answer again, so moving forward is safe. The stopping position is the first IP numbered ≥p with count 1 (a new IP has count at least 1); combined with the invariant, it is the earliest-appearing of all unique IPs. Going out of range means no unique IP exists, and the answer is the empty string.

## Complexity

Each ADD performs one hash lookup; the pointer moves at most "number of distinct IPs" times in total, so the total expected time is O(total number of characters), and the space is O(total length of the distinct IPs).

## Independent verification

The oracle keeps the current unique IPs in an ordered dictionary (deleting an IP on its second appearance) and answers a query with the first key, without reusing the pointer approach. For small domains, a separate brute force over the history recounts all earlier ADDs at every query and finds the first IP with count 1 in order of first appearance; on three IPs (two of which differ only in case), every command sequence of length 1..6 is enumerated, and the reference program is actually run on each. The formal cases cover the original examples, empty answers, case differences, long pointer jumps, a million distinct IPs, high-collision random data and more. Four wrong programs that exit normally (ignoring counts, treating an IP as non-unique only at three visits, not printing an empty line for an empty answer, ignoring case) are each judged wrong on the formal cases.
